subject: math
cluster: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples
intro: Eight multiple-choice questions on dividing multi-digit whole numbers with the standard algorithm. Choose the single best answer for each.

items.prompt:
Divide using the standard algorithm: $1{,}512 \div 6$.
A) $0$
B) $252$
C) $250$
D) $262$

steps: Long division: $6$ into $15$ is $2$ ($2 \times 6 = 12$), remainder $3$; bring down $1$ to make $31$.
$6$ into $31$ is $5$ ($5 \times 6 = 30$), remainder $1$; bring down $2$ to make $12$.
$6$ into $12$ is $2$ ($2 \times 6 = 12$), remainder $0$. The quotient is $252$.
Check: $252 \times 6 = 1{,}512$. So B is correct.
A ($0$) comes from reversing dividend and divisor and computing $6 \div 1{,}512$ instead. C ($250$) and D ($262$) come from a single-digit slip in one quotient digit.

items.prompt:
Divide using the standard algorithm: $864 \div 4$.
A) $206$
B) $217$
C) $216$
D) $0$

steps: $4$ into $8$ is $2$ ($2 \times 4 = 8$), remainder $0$; bring down $6$ to make $6$.
$4$ into $6$ is $1$ ($1 \times 4 = 4$), remainder $2$; bring down $4$ to make $24$.
$4$ into $24$ is $6$ ($6 \times 4 = 24$), remainder $0$. The quotient is $216$.
Check: $216 \times 4 = 864$. So C is correct.
A ($206$) drops the tens digit, inserting a wrong $0$. B ($217$) is an off-by-one slip on the last digit. D ($0$) reverses dividend and divisor.

items.prompt:
Divide using the standard algorithm: $2{,}345 \div 5$.
A) $469$
B) $0$
C) $479$
D) $409$

steps: $5$ into $23$ is $4$ ($4 \times 5 = 20$), remainder $3$; bring down $4$ to make $34$.
$5$ into $34$ is $6$ ($6 \times 5 = 30$), remainder $4$; bring down $5$ to make $45$.
$5$ into $45$ is $9$ ($9 \times 5 = 45$), remainder $0$. The quotient is $469$.
Check: $469 \times 5 = 2{,}345$. So A is correct.
B ($0$) reverses dividend and divisor. C ($479$) is a single-digit estimation slip. D ($409$) wrongly inserts a $0$ in the tens place.

items.prompt:
Divide using the standard algorithm: $6{,}018 \div 3$.
A) $216$
B) $2{,}060$
C) $2{,}016$
D) $2{,}006$

steps: $3$ into $6$ is $2$, remainder $0$; bring down $0$ to make $0$.
$3$ into $0$ is $0$ (write a $0$ in the tens place of the quotient); bring down $1$ to make $1$.
$3$ into $1$ is $0$ (write a $0$); bring down $8$ to make $18$. $3$ into $18$ is $6$, remainder $0$.
Reading the quotient digits gives $2{,}006$. Check: $2{,}006 \times 3 = 6{,}018$. So D is correct.
A ($216$) omits the needed $0$s in the quotient, shortening it. B ($2{,}060$) and C ($2{,}016$) misplace a single $0$ digit.

items.prompt:
Divide using the standard algorithm: $4{,}827 \div 23$.
A) $29\text{ R }20$
B) $209\text{ R }20$
C) $20920$
D) $210\text{ R }20$

steps: $23$ into $48$ is $2$ ($2 \times 23 = 46$), remainder $2$; bring down $2$ to make $22$.
$23$ into $22$ is $0$ (write a $0$ in the quotient); bring down $7$ to make $227$.
$23$ into $227$ is $9$ ($9 \times 23 = 207$), remainder $20$. The quotient is $209$ with remainder $20$.
Check: $209 \times 23 + 20 = 4{,}807 + 20 = 4{,}827$. So B is correct.
A ($29$) drops the interior $0$ from misalignment. C ($20920$) jams the remainder onto the quotient instead of writing R. D ($210$) is an off-by-one estimation slip.

items.prompt:
Which multiplication correctly checks that $7{,}854 \div 34 = 231$?
A) $231 \times 34 = 7{,}888$
B) $34 \times 7{,}854 = 231$
C) $231 \times 34 = 7{,}854$
D) $231 + 34 = 7{,}854$

steps: To check a division with remainder $0$, multiply the quotient by the divisor: $\text{quotient} \times \text{divisor} = \text{dividend}$.
Since $231 \times 34 = 7{,}854$, the division is verified. So C is correct.
A uses a wrong product ($7{,}888$ reflects an estimation slip giving $232$). B reverses the roles of dividend and quotient. D adds instead of multiplying.

items.prompt:
A school packs $3{,}458$ pencils into boxes of $24$. How many full boxes are filled and how many pencils are left over?
A) $143$ full boxes, $26$ left over
B) $144$ full boxes, $2$ left over
C) $145$ full boxes, $0$ left over
D) $144$ full boxes, $0$ left over

steps: Divide $3{,}458 \div 24$. $24$ into $34$ is $1$ ($24$), remainder $10$; bring down $5$ to make $105$.
$24$ into $105$ is $4$ ($4 \times 24 = 96$), remainder $9$; bring down $8$ to make $98$.
Check: $144 \times 24 + 2 = 3{,}456 + 2 = 3{,}458$. So $144$ full boxes with $2$ pencils left over, which is B.
A ($143\text{ R }26$) stops subtracting too early; since $26 > 24$ another box can still be filled. C ($145$) rounds up incorrectly. D ignores the nonzero remainder.

items.prompt:
Divide using the standard algorithm: $34{,}820 \div 67$.
A) $59\text{ R }47$
B) $520\text{ R }47$
C) $519\text{ R }47$
D) $51947$

steps: $67$ into $348$ is $5$ ($5 \times 67 = 335$), remainder $13$; bring down $2$ to make $132$.
$67$ into $132$ is $1$ ($1 \times 67 = 67$), remainder $65$; bring down $0$ to make $650$.
$67$ into $650$ is $9$ ($9 \times 67 = 603$), remainder $47$. The quotient is $519$ with remainder $47$.
A ($59$) drops a quotient digit from misalignment. B ($520$) is an off-by-one estimation slip. D ($51947$) jams the remainder onto the quotient instead of writing R.
